source_text: Sed post haec admoves sententiam tibi caram et dicis: Si autem naturae humanae mali nihil inesset, salvanda non esset. Qui ergo dicit eam bonum non esse, bonum negat conditae Creatorem; qui vero negat ei malum inesse, misericordem vitiatae invidet Salvatorem [n247] . Sit igitur lector intentus, videbit nihil te dixisse aliud, quam quod dicendum negaras; pronuntiasti enim ei rei malum inesse naturaliter, quam dixeras malam non esse naturaliter.
pass_a_gloss: But after these you move a sentence dear to you and say: But if nothing of evil were in human nature, it would not be to be saved. Whoever therefore says it is not a good denies a good Creator of the founded; but whoever denies evil is in it begrudges a merciful Savior to the vitiated. Let the reader therefore be intent; he will see you have said nothing other than what you had denied must be said; for you have pronounced evil to be in that thing naturally which you had said was not naturally evil.

lemmas.lexica: LS naturalis; Blaise malum naturale=evil as a nature
LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS bonum; Blaise good-of-nature vs good-of-will
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: But afterward you introduce the statement dear to you: ‘If no evil were within human nature, it would not need to be saved. Whoever says it is not good denies a good Creator to the nature created; whoever denies it contains evil begrudges a merciful Savior to the nature corrupted’ (Augustine, Marriage and Sexual Desire 2.36). Let the reader pay attention: you will see that he has said nothing other than what he had denied should be said. You have pronounced evil naturally present in the very thing you said was not naturally evil.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
